name: Stellmark Concord Overcoat
description:
A long, structured overcoat in charcoal, navy, or camel — the kind that says you have somewhere to be and it matters. The Stellmark Concord is cut from a wool-polyester blend that drapes well and resists wrinkling even after a full day in a pressurized transit pod. The lapels are moderate, the buttons are real horn, and the silhouette is classic double-breasted with a subtle waist suppression. Nothing about it is loud. Everything about it is intentional.

Stellmark is a Tier 4 clothier that occupies the space between bespoke tailoring and corporate retail — expensive enough to signal success, accessible enough that mid-level executives can justify it on an expense account. The Concord is their anchor product. It's the coat a Tier 3 professional buys when they get promoted and a Tier 4 executive replaces every three years without thinking about it.
what_it_says: You've arrived, or you're very convincingly pretending to have arrived.
story_hooks: Two executives at a merger negotiation are wearing identical Stellmark Concords — one of them is not who they claim to be.
A Stellmark tailor has been quietly altering coats for clients who want hidden document pockets — and has been keeping copies of everything passed through them.
A Tier 2 knockoff of the Concord is being sold in the working-class markets; it's nearly identical, and someone at Stellmark is furious enough to hire investigators.
